transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 08:23 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO, SummitPay), Sofia Alvarez (Eng Mgr), Anita Patel (DevOps)

Summary (auto-generated): Quick quick summary - walkthrough of Optimize features focusing on batching and KV/prefix cache strategies. A lot of numbers and tradeoffs, we sketched cost model for their fraud detection traffic.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood. Priya's here on the call to walk through Optimize recommendations. Marcus, Sofia, Anita, thanks for making time.
[00:16] Marcus Lee: Hey Alex, thanks, excited to see what you got. We're trying to reduce token costs while keeping sub-200ms tail latency for our fraud scoring path.
[00:27] Priya Nair: Yeah cool, quick show of hands — are most requests short, like 128 tokens, or do you have long context traces?
[00:33] Sofia Alvarez: This is Sofia. Most are short, like 80–150 tokens, but we have some long sessions with device logs where it goes to 2k tokens. Those are less frequent.
[00:44] Anita Patel: Annap—we have retention requirement too, we can't send PII offsite. So Private/Dedicated is interesting; but first we wanna see cost delta.
[00:54] Alex Chen: Totally understood. Priya, do you wanna share the Optimize slide? (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/optimize/pilot) — I'll paste after.
[01:04] Priya Nair: Yep, sharing screen now. Alright first slide — workload profile. So we asked for sample traces, and we looked at seq length histogram. For SummitPay it's heavy at 128 tokens and a long tail at 2k.
[01:22] Marcus Lee: Correct. Also we have bursty traffic at end of day — throughput spikes 4x for a few minutes.
[01:31] Priya Nair: Good to know. So two levers we recommend: batching (to amortize per-token cost and throughput) and KV/prefix caching to avoid re-computing prefixes across sessions.
[01:41] Sofia Alvarez: Can you remind us how KV cache helps? I always confuse prefix cache and KV.
[01:48] Priya Nair: Sure — prefix cache stores the model's hidden states (key/value cache) for a given input prefix so repeated prompts that share the same prefix can skip recomputation. It's super effective when many requests have identical or very similar prefixes, e.g., standard system prompt + fixed fields.
[02:06] Marcus Lee: Our fraud scoring has a fixed schema prompt plus user events appended, so sounds promising.
[02:13] Alex Chen: We ran an example cost model — baseline Hosted (no caching, small batch) vs with batching+KV. I'll read numbers — caveat transcription: end up rounding. Baseline cost estimate: $0.18 per 1k tokens; with batching+kv we estimated effective cost down to $0.05 per 1k on our sample traffic assuming 40% cache hit rate.
[02:44] Anita Patel: Wait 40% hit rate, that's optimistic. How sensitive is the model to hit rate?
[02:49] Priya Nair: Great question. We have a sensitivity table — at 20% hit rate savings is modest ~15–20% cost reduction; at 60% it gets to ~60% cost reduction. We'll share the spreadsheet.
[03:03] Marcus Lee: What's the impact on latency? We can't add big batching delays.
[03:08] Priya Nair: Right — tradeoff: bigger batch sizes reduce cost but increase latency. For sub-200ms SLO, we recommended micro-batching: batch size up to 8 with batching delay 1–3 ms, plus async tail-handling. For your short requests, that keeps p95 under 200ms in our benchmarks.
[03:28] Sofia Alvarez: Are these numbers on Hosted or Dedicated?
[03:31] Priya Nair: Those bench numbers are on Redwood Dedicated (NVIDIA H100 equivalent). On Hosted we can still apply batching but performance varies by instance. Dedicated gives predictable latency and better throughput.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: For compliance we likely need Private — can you support the same optimizations on Private?
[03:46] Alex Chen: Yes — the runtime is the same across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. Batching and KV cache features are in the runtime and available on all deployment modes. The only difference is the underlying infra and network topology.
[03:58] Anita Patel: We need KMS integration and audit logs — are those included in Private?
[04:03] Alex Chen: Yes — we have KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging. We'll attach security docs (SOC2 and network requirements) after the call.
[04:12] Priya Nair: Back to cost model: example scenario — 1M requests/day, avg 120 tokens, baseline cost ~ $22k/month; with batching + 40% KV hit it dropped to ~$6k/month in our simplified model. These assume model TCO and token pricing placeholders — actual numbers vary with model choice and quantization.
[04:33] Marcus Lee: You mentioned quantization — does that change KV cache behavior?
[04:38] Priya Nair: Behavior is same; quantized kernels affect model speed and token cost but cache semantics unchanged. There is sometimes a small perf delta when using int8 kernels but we account for that in the bench.
[04:51] Sofia Alvarez: Can we see a concrete example of prefix similarity for our logs?
[04:55] Priya Nair: Sure — Priya pastes example: "SYSTEM: /fraud/score schema fields..." repeated across requests. That's a high-value prefix to cache. Also we suggested normalizing variable fields so more requests hit the cache.
[05:12] Marcus Lee: Normalizing how? Strip timestamps and device IDs before sending?
[05:16] Priya Nair: Exactly — pre-process to canonicalize non-informative fields. We can provide guidelines.
[05:22] Alex Chen: Quick note on batching: we support dynamic batching in the runtime — it groups requests by model and sequence-length bucket to avoid padding explosion. We recommended two buckets for you: short (<=256) and long (>256).
[05:38] Anita Patel: What's the implementation lift? Our infra team worries about SDK changes.
[05:42] Priya Nair: Minimal. The SDK supports batch endpoints — you can either send single requests and rely on server-side continuous batching, or use client-side multi-request batching. For cache, you need to set a cache key (we use hash of canonicalized prefix). We'll share code snippets.
[06:00] Alex Chen: I'll paste the snippet after — (link: github.com/redwood/examples/kv-cache) note in chat
[06:07] Priya Nair: Now latency/cost tradeoff graph — (screen) at 0ms delay cost is higher p95 lower; at 10ms delay cost halves but p95 pushes up. For your SLO we suggest 1–3ms.
[06:24] Marcus Lee: Could we do canary rollout to test customer-facing traffic?
[06:28] Priya Nair: Yes — Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback. For the pilot we usually route 10% traffic for two days, measure quality and latency.
[06:38] Sofia Alvarez: About quality — do caches affect model outputs? Are we risking drift?
[06:44] Priya Nair: KV caching only avoids re-computation of past tokens; outputs are identical if the prefix is identical. The risk is if canonicalization changes prompt meaning; that's why we validate on a dev set.
[06:58] Marcus Lee: One more question: how do you calculate the 40% hit rate — that seems made-up.
[07:03] Priya Nair: We used your traces — we matched on canonicalized prefixes and counted repeats. It's an estimate; actual will vary. We'll run the same matching on full logs during the pilot.
[07:15] Anita Patel: Network egress costs — any effect if we run Dedicated vs Private?
[07:20] Alex Chen: Private keeps data in your VPC so egress is internal; Hosted may incur cloud egress depending on region. We'll include network notes in the security pack.
[07:31] Priya Nair: OK quick demo of Optimize console — showing per-route token breakdown, cache hit metrics, and batch histograms. (Priya clicks) Here you can see cache hit rate over time, probe for top prefixes, and simulate cost change by adjusting hit rate slider.
[07:49] Sophia (sic): Sorry, that's Sofia. The console UI looks useful — can we export the cost model as CSV?
[07:54] Priya Nair: Yes, export and API endpoints are available.
[07:58] Marcus Lee: For pilot infra, do you need host access or logs?
[08:01] Priya Nair: We'll ask for sample traces and a short-term service account to fetch metrics if you want deeper integrations. But initial pilot can run with just sample traces and API keys.
[08:12] Alex Chen: Recap and next steps — we'll send the cost spreadsheet, security docs, and a step-by-step pilot playbook. SE will run a benchmark with your traces and share latency/cost numbers.
[08:24] Marcus Lee: Great. Let's plan to kick off pilot mid next week.
[08:28] Alex Chen: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[08:31] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks, bye.
[08:32] Anita Patel: Bye.
